bg-33-01.hint: I bought apples and pears at the market.
bg-33-01.why: Listing nouns with -와 (after vowel) and -과 (after consonant): 사과와 배.

bg-33-01.q: Write a sentence saying you watched a movie with a friend using 친구랑 and 영화를.
bg-33-01.why: 친구 takes -(이)랑 to indicate companion in casual conversation: 친구랑.

steps.en: I ate a meal with a friend.
Yesterday at the restaurant, I ate a delicious meal with a friend.

ko: 토요일 오후에 동생과 함께 대형 마트에 장을 보러 갔어요.
신선한 사과와 딸기, 그리고 과자하고 음료수를 카트에 담았어요.
집에 돌아와서 가족들과 맛있는 간식을 나누어 먹었어요.
en: On Saturday afternoon, I went grocery shopping at a hypermarket with my younger sibling.
We put fresh apples and strawberries, and snacks and drinks into the cart.
Coming home, we shared and ate delicious snacks with family.

bg-33-01.q: Who did the writer go shopping with?
bg-33-01.why: The text says '동생과 함께 대형 마트에 장을 보러 갔어요'.

bg-33-01.q: What fruits did they put in the cart?

items: I can connect multiple nouns using -와/과 (formal), -하고 (neutral), and -(이)랑 (casual).
I can express doing activities together with someone using companionship particles.

bg-33-02.hint: Yesterday I was tired, so I slept as much as 10 hours.
bg-33-02.why: Attached to quantities, -(이)나 expresses surprise at a large amount: 10시간이나.

bg-33-02.q: Write a sentence offering a choice between water and juice using 물이나 and 주스를.
bg-33-02.why: 물 ends in ㄹ batchim, taking -이나 to mean 'water or ...': 물이나.

bg-33-02.h: -(이)나 Choice ('Or') vs Quantity Surprise ('As much as')

a.d: Placed between nouns to offer or suggest one option among alternatives.
ex: 주말에 영화**나** 책을 봐요. / I watch a movie or read a book on weekends.

b.d: Placed after a number or counter to express that the amount is surprisingly large.
ex: 사과를 5개**나** 먹었어요! / I ate as many as 5 apples!

bg-33-02.tip: When attached to nouns it means 'or'; when attached to counting numbers it means 'wow, that many!'.

base.en: I slept as much as 10 hours.

steps.en: Yesterday I slept as much as 10 hours.
Yesterday because I was so tired, I slept deeply as much as 10 hours.

ko: 주말에 친구를 만나러 카페에 갔는데 사람이 정말 많았어요.
겨우 자리에 앉아서 시원한 커피나 음료수를 마시며 이야기했어요.
en: On the weekend I went to a cafe to meet a friend, and there were really a lot of people.
Since there were no seats, we had to wait outside for as long as 30 minutes.
Finally sitting down, we talked while drinking iced coffee or beverages.

bg-33-02.q: How long did they have to wait outside?
What did they drink once they got a seat?
bg-33-02.why: The text says '시원한 커피나 음료수를 마시며'.

items: I can offer alternatives using -(이)나 (or) with batchim distinction.
I can express surprise at surprisingly large quantities or durations using -(이)나.

bg-33-03.hint: Every weekend I ride a bicycle in the park.

bg-33-03.q: Write a sentence saying you also study Korean using 저도 and 한국어를.
bg-33-03.why: 도 replaces subject particles (은/는): 저도 (not 저는도).

steps.en: Every weekend I ride a bicycle.
Every weekend in the park, I ride a bicycle excitedly.

ko: 우리 반에는 여러 나라에서 온 유학생들이 모여 있어요.
나라마다 모국어와 인사법은 다르지만 모두 한국어를 열심히 배워요.
저도 친구들과 함께 매일 아침마다 도서관에 가서 예습을 해요.
en: In our class, international students from various countries have gathered.
Each country has different native languages and greetings, but everyone studies Korean hard.
I also go to the library every morning with friends to prepare lessons.

bg-33-03.q: What differs across the students' home countries?
bg-33-03.why: The text states '나라마다 모국어와 인사법은 다르지만'.

bg-33-03.q: When does the writer go to the library?
bg-33-03.why: The text says '매일 아침마다 도서관에 가서'.

items: I can use -도 (also/too) correctly replacing topic and object markers.
I can express recurring routines using -마다 (every/each).

bg-33-04.hint: Every morning I drink warm coffee or tea.
bg-33-04.why: Recurring frequency takes -마다 (아침마다) and choice takes -나 (차나/커피나).

bg-33-04.q: Write a sentence saying you also like Korean food using 저도 and 한국 음식을.
bg-33-04.why: Inclusion particle -도 replaces 는: 저도 한국 음식을 아주 좋아해요.

bg-33-04.q: Fix the double particle error combining 는 and 도.
bg-33-04.hint: The particle 도 completely replaces 는: 저도.
bg-33-04.why: Never combine topic marker 는 with 도. Use 저도: 저도 한국 드라마를 매일 봐요.

a.d: Includes both elements together (A and B are both selected or involved).
ex: 사과**와** 배를 모두 사요. / I buy both apples and pears.

b.d: Selects one option among alternatives (either A or B).
ex: 사과**나** 배를 하나만 사요. / I buy either an apple or a pear.

bg-33-04.tip: -와/과 means BOTH together; -(이)나 means EITHER one among choices.

steps.en: I also like that exciting song really very much.

ko: 저는 주말마다 친구와 함께 시내 중심가에 나가요.
점심에는 가볍게 김밥이나 떡볶이를 사 먹고 서점에 들러요.
친구도 책 읽는 것을 좋아해서 우리는 함께 즐거운 시간을 보내요.
en: Every weekend I go downtown with a friend.
For lunch, we lightly buy and eat gimbap or tteokbokki and stop by a bookstore.
My friend also likes reading books, so we spend an enjoyable time together.

bg-33-04.q: What do they usually eat lightly for lunch?
bg-33-04.why: The text says '김밥이나 떡볶이를 사 먹고'.

bg-33-04.q: What does the friend also like doing?
bg-33-04.why: The passage notes '친구도 책 읽는 것을 좋아해서'.

items: I can clearly distinguish between listing both items (-와/과) and choosing one (-(이)나).
I can correctly apply -도 without particle stacking errors, and describe regular routines with -마다.
